structural_assimilation.question: How far has the theory increment travelled through the repository's structure?
active_complete_requires: EA-1 a SRT native proposition, guardrail or registered tension exists
EA-2 it has entered an appropriate active owner
EA-3 a real retrieval path resolves to it
EA-4 a fast layer or default load path can read it
EA-5 the superseded formulation has been handled
structural_assimilation.note: Structure only. Says nothing about whether any AI ever retrieved or used it.

behavioral_availability.question: Has a fresh session been observed retrieving this node and using it to judge? ABSOLUTE, never compared to a baseline.

value_definitions.observed: retrieved and used in at least one recorded run, under any retrieval mode
value_definitions.robustly_observed: retrieved and used in at least two independent BOUNDED runs (see SRT_BOUNDED_RETRIEVAL_PROTOCOL_2026-08-08.md)
value_definitions.failed: a recorded run did not retrieve it, or retrieved it and judged wrongly

behavioral_availability.note: A zero intervention effect is NOT evidence against behavioral availability. If a baseline already retrieves and uses the node, that is availability, not ineffectiveness. Only a recorded run may set this; CI never can.

intervention_effect.question: What did one specific PR or writeback add relative to its own baseline? Per-intervention, not a node property.
intervention_effect.note: Recorded in the node's `interventions` list. A single field may never carry both 'the node works' and 'this PR helped'.

derived_status_rule: effectively_assimilated := structural_assimilation == 'active_complete' AND behavioral_availability in {'observed','robustly_observed'}. It is a claim about THE NODE (is this theory structurally in place and actually used?), NOT a claim about any PR. Whether a given PR added anything lives only in that PR's intervention_effect record. Computed, never stored.
